newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert wants to ban Cablevision deal.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert wants to ban Cablevision deal.

text.p: European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Thursday he would propose next week that the Commission ban Cablevision, the Spanish cable television deal between Telefonica de Espana and Canal Plus.
"I am going to propose to my colleagues next week to take a negative decision," Van Miert told a conference.

The EU's advisory committee on mergers concluded earlier this week that the joint venture should be blocked on the grounds it would create a dominant position in the Spanish market. Spain was the only dissenting voice on the committee.
The Commission must take a final decision on the operation by November 26. However, it could be spared the ruling if the parent companies took the initiative and withdrew the deal.
Commission sources said earlier this week that Telefonica may do that to avoid a negative ruling.
Company sources told the daily El Mundo last week Telefonica's directors would recommend the dissolution of Cablevision at the next board meeting on November 11.

But Sogecable, its partner in the venture which belongs to Canal Plus France and Spain's Promotora de Informaciones SA, was more reluctant to abandon the plan, the sources said, speculating that it might seek compensation from Telefonica.
The joint venture was set up by Telefonica and Sogecable SA in July 1995 to operate and distribute pay television and multimedia in Spain via cable TV networks.
Sogecable and Canal Plus Espana, a subsidiary of the French company, are both in the fast-growing pay-television business and Telefonica is the country's dominant telecoms operator.
Ten million households have televisions in Spain but only 200,000 have access to cable, making it one of the largest untapped markets left in western Europe.
When it began a full probe into the case in July, the Commission expressed strong doubts about it because Telefonica still has a monopoly on the local telecommunications market.
The operation would affect the market for cable television services and would also have an indirect impact on the telephone and data transmission sectors, it said at the time.
The Commission, which vets all major corporate agreements which affect trade in the EU, has become increasingly tough on media alliances and especially on cable pay-television deals.
